title: Canonical multiplication into a normalized reduced tensor algebra
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings with an $A$-algebra structure on $B$. Let $K,L,P$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension], with compatible algebra structures $A\to K$, $A\to L$, $B\to L$, $K\to L$, $K\to P$ and $A\to P$: the composites $A\to B\to L$ and $A\to K\to L$ are the given $A\to L$, and $A\to K\to P$ is the given $A\to P$. Put $R_P=\operatorname{Int}_A(P)$ and $C_P=\operatorname{Int}_B((L\otimes_KP)/\sqrt{(0)})$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], where $\sqrt{(0)}$ is the ideal of all nilpotent elements. The canonical multiplication homomorphism $\mu_P:B\otimes_AR_P\to C_P$ sends $b\otimes r$ to the class of $(b\otimes1)(1\otimes r)$ in the reduced tensor algebra. This class is integral over $B$, since $r$ is integral over $A$. Its restriction to $1\otimes R_P$ is the canonical normalization map $\nu_P:R_P\to C_P$, $r\mapsto[1\otimes r]$.
